subject: Post-demo: Zephyr latency & throughput follow-up — AB run plan
body:
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Lopez <sara.lopez@zephyr.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 27 Mar 2029 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: Zephyr latency & throughput follow-up — AB run plan

Hi Sara,

Thanks again for taking the demo today — appreciate the team's time and the candid discussion on production constraints. Per our call, the primary concern from Zephyr was predictable p95/p99 latency for short prompt interactions and end-to-end tokens/sec for larger batched workloads. Attached I dropped a small sample of the workload traces you promised (zephyr-workload-samples.json) and a short comparison matrix we sketched versus the hyperscaler you mentioned (redwood-vs-hypercloud-quick-matrix.pdf).

Proposed next steps (short and actionable):
- Run an A/B pair of benchmark jobs over the next 48 hours: Redwood hosted model X (quantized) vs Hyperscaler endpoint (your current prod config).
- Two canonical scenarios:
  1) Low-latency interactive: 1-2 prompt tokens avg, sequence length 64, target p95 < 120ms and p99 < 250ms.
  2) Batch throughput: concurrent 16-stream batching, typical sequence length 512, tokens/sec and cost-per-1M tokens comparison.
- We'll capture p50/p95/p99, tail variance, KV-cache hit rates, and tokens/sec measured from both sides.
- Share run configs (we attached suggested run variants in the .xlsx) and schedule the runs — can you confirm a 2-hour window on Thurs morning PT?

If that works I’ll loop in Karthik and Monica to lock the exact runner config and post-run analysis.

Thanks,
Michael

--
Michael Grant
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
michael.grant@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

---

From: Sara Lopez <sara.lopez@zephyr.ai>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
Cc: DevOps Team <eng-ops@zephyr.ai>, Zephyr Procurement <procure@zephyr.ai>
Date: Wed, 27 Mar 2029 12:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Zephyr latency & throughput follow-up — AB run plan

Thanks Michael — that aligns with what we discussed internally. Thu 28 Mar 09:30-11:30 PT works for the DevOps team to run the pair of tests (we'll reserve a maintenance window). I've attached our sample traces in the Google Drive folder I shared in the call. Quick clarifications:

- For the hyperscaler baseline we will use their on-demand c6i-like instance + their managed endpoint with default batching. We will also run a variant with their optimized batching.
- For Redwood: please confirm the model variant you intend to use and whether the quantized path will be identical to the demo (8-bit KF).
- We are most interested in the p99 tail under 95th percentile load — so please make sure the run harness can simulate short bursts.

Sara
Sara Lopez
Head of Engineering, Zephyr Analytics
sara.lopez@zephyr.ai

---

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 28 Mar 2029 07:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Zephyr latency & throughput follow-up — AB run plan

Adding the bench plan details for internal alignment before we post to Zephyr:

Bench variants (we will run each against Zephyr baseline):
- Interactive (INT): seq_len=64, prompt_median_tokens=3, concurrency=8, batching_window=8ms, model=redwood-x-8q (KV cache warm path)
- Interactive (INT-swap): same but model=redwood-x-fp16 (to measure quantization delta)
- Throughput (TP): seq_len=512, avg_prompt=48 tokens, streaming disabled, concurrency=16 streams, batching_window=32ms, model=redwood-x-8q
- Stress (TAIL): repeated 1s bursts of 100 reqs for 3 mins to measure p99 under bursty load

Metrics to collect (automated):
- p50/p90/p95/p99 latencies, tokens/sec, percent time spent in kernel vs overhead, cost-estimate per 1M tokens, KV-cache hit ratio, and memory/GC events if any.

Runner notes: use our runner v2.4 which supports identical request shaping and header propagation so Zephyr can reconcile traces. Attach the configs we plan to run to the external message.

I'll open the test jobs and attach the run-configs to the sheet. Monica, can you verify the cost-estimator assumptions in the spreadsheet?

- Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference

---

From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Lopez <sara.lopez@zephyr.ai>, DevOps Team <eng-ops@zephyr.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 28 Mar 2029 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Zephyr latency & throughput follow-up — AB run plan

Sara — great, thanks for confirming the window. Quick confirmations on our side:
- Model: redwood-x-8q for the primary runs; INT-swap will use redwood-x-fp16. Quantized path is the same as the demo (8-bit KF path).
- Runner: Redwood runner v2.4 (we'll provide the exact Docker image tag in the Drive).
- Attachments: zephyr-workload-samples.json, redwood-vs-hypercloud-quick-matrix.pdf, zephyr-benchmark-schedule.xlsx (schedule + config).

We will:
1) Kick off Redwood runs at 09:30 PT and stream metrics to the Drive folder.
2) Ask Zephyr to run the hyperscaler baseline at the same window and drop their raw traces (timestamp-aligned).
3) Post-run: Karthik and Naomi will do a 60-minute readout to compare p95/p99, tokens/sec, and cost; we will capture a short decision memo and recommended next bench if we see >15% delta on p95 or >20% delta on tokens/sec.

Naomi — can you schedule the 60-minute readout for Thu 29 Mar 09:00 PT?

Thanks — looking forward to clean numbers.

Michael
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

---

From: Sara Lopez <sara.lopez@zephyr.ai>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
Cc: DevOps Team <eng-ops@zephyr.ai>, Zephyr Procurement <procure@zephyr.ai>
Date: Fri, 29 Mar 2029 16:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Zephyr latency & throughput follow-up — AB run plan

Michael — runs completed and baseline traces uploaded to the Drive folder. Preliminary notes: p95 difference looks small for INT (Redwood slightly faster on median), but we see a sustained tokens/sec delta in TP that may justify the deeper follow-up you proposed. We'll join the readout tomorrow.

Sara
